guidance.procedure: After deciding the relation, collect every complete responsive member: the operative sentence plus any governing lead-in, definition introduction, exception introduction, or continuation needed to express its force, actor, object, trigger, or scope. Include repeated provisions that independently resolve the hypothesis. Exclude headings, neighboring examples, generic security or duration language, and clauses that are merely useful context.

Read the operative ban, its exceptions, recipient definitions, and access obligations together. Authorization for consultants, agents, advisers, contractors, affiliates, or other representatives supports sharing with some third parties; access language covering agents or representatives may complete an employee exception. Employee/officer-only access followed by a ban on everyone else opposes it, as does a bare outside-recipient ban. Merely describing a signer as an employee or agent, or the owner directly granting that individual access, does not authorize the receiving party and leaves the hypothesis unresolved.

Evaluate what may remain after the stated return or destruction is completed. An express archive, backup, legal-retention, dispute, or records exception supports possession. An exhaustive duty covering all protected information and all copies, or an express no-retention sentence, opposes it. A duty covering only tangible documents or another specified subset, without saying nothing else may remain, is unresolved. Thus “return all records and copies; retain none” opposes, while “return tangible materials” alone does not.

Match the duty to an ending event, not merely the word “termination.” Return or destruction triggered by termination or expiration, conclusion of services or a project, ending discussions, abandoning the contemplated transaction, or a scheduled final-return deadline after the agreement term supports the hypothesis. A request-only duty during an otherwise continuing relationship is unresolved. Include the ending-event language and every operative return/destruction limb.

Separate agreement duration from the duration of substantive duties. “These duties survive termination” supports survival. “The agreement remains effective for five years” alone is unresolved. A clause confining the confidentiality or use duties themselves to a fixed period from the effective date, with no post-termination continuation, opposes survival; for example, “the confidentiality obligations extend only five years from signing.” Enforcement, indemnity, severability, or remedy language does not become survival merely because it can be invoked later.

Inspect the operative protected-information definition, including a recital that directly declares the defined object. A formulation such as “the technical information described below is Confidential Information” supports technical-only coverage even without repeating “only.” Express business, financial, commercial, personnel, customer, or similar nontechnical categories oppose it. Mere background that parties possess technical or commercial material, or a generic definition such as “all information” without an identifiable content category, leaves the proposition unresolved.

Test whether every protected item must be affirmatively identified to the recipient. Marking, contemporaneous designation, later written confirmation, or the discloser expressly making the recipient aware can support the universal condition. Coverage “whether or not marked,” or based only on what a reasonable recipient should understand, opposes it. A broad definition, an authority’s general classification scheme, or the discloser merely considering information confidential does not itself communicate an identification for every disclosure and is unresolved. Include the complete governing identification sequence.

Require an operative statement about conveyance mode. “Information transmitted verbally, in writing, or electronically,” when it defines the protected object, supports oral coverage, as do explicit oral, spoken, or verbal terms and comprehensive tangible/intangible formulations. References merely to discussions, information learned, agreement content, or information “in any form” within a subject-matter list do not establish verbal disclosure. If oral protection depends on designation or written confirmation, include the responsive condition sequence.

Require a specific independent-development provision, ordinarily stating development without use of, reference to, or access to protected information. A generic exclusions lead-in is responsive evidence only when paired with that particular limb. Public-domain, third-party-source, compelled-disclosure, nondisclosure, nonuse, or copying language alone neither permits nor prohibits independent development and leaves the issue unresolved. A direct ban on independent development would oppose the hypothesis.

Look for an incoming-source rule: information may be received, obtained, furnished, or acquired from a lawful third party not bound by confidentiality or other transmission restrictions. Pair the specific source limb with its governing exclusion introduction and stated conditions. A generic exception introduction, a legal-demand clause, an outgoing third-party disclosure rule, or an independent-development limb does not address acquisition and is unresolved. For example, “received from an unrestricted outside source” supports; “may disclose when compelled” does not.

Distinguish permission, a blanket ban, and a restriction on copying manner. “May copy” or “shall not copy except as necessary” supports; an unqualified “shall not copy” opposes. A rule only forbidding copies that obscure markings, or regulating the form or handling of copies, leaves general permission unresolved. If one grammatical exception governs a series such as “do not copy or disclose except to necessary employees,” it can support copying within that exception. Include the undertaking lead-in when it supplies actor or force.

Find both legal compulsion and mandatory warning. A pattern such as “when disclosure is required by law, notify the discloser before releasing the information” supports the hypothesis even without a separately labeled compelled-disclosure exception. Permission to comply with law without notice is unresolved. Include the trigger and notice sentence; when the notice is a proviso referring to listed legal processes, include the governing lead-in and all referenced limbs needed to identify the compelled event, but omit unrelated disclosure permissions.

Require an operative allowance for the receiving party to disclose or provide access to its employees, usually subject to need-to-know or purpose limits. A statement that a designated signer happens to be an employee, officer, agent, or consultant describes status rather than authorizing the receiving party to share and leaves the issue unresolved. Permission only for outside advisers does not establish employee sharing; a general disclosure ban without an employee exception also remains unresolved unless it expressly covers and forbids employees.

Collect every provision that independently limits use to the stated purpose or forbids other use, including a governing purpose clause and repeated nonuse provisions. Exclude headings, disclosure/security duties, and a pure ownership or no-license clause. However, a construction clause stating that no license exists except a limited right to use solely for the stated purpose independently expresses the use limit and is responsive. After finding one restriction, scan the whole contract for a second operative restriction rather than stopping at the first candidate.

Support the hypothesis with an express denial of license, title, proprietary right, right of use, or other interest. A limited permission to review or use information for the stated purpose does not by itself oppose this no-proprietary-right proposition. Sole-and-exclusive ownership coupled with mandatory return can independently deny the recipient an interest; mere identification of the owner cannot. Include a linked construction lead-in and subordinate denial, and include each separate clause that independently denies rights.

Inspect whether the agreement’s existence, negotiation, terms, content, discussions, or expressly designated subject matter is itself confidential or non-disclosable. Such language supports the hypothesis. A generic entire-agreement clause, confidentiality of exchanged business information, or a reference to discussions that does not protect their existence leaves it unresolved. Express authorization to disclose the fact of the agreement would oppose it. Include the definition lead-in when it is what makes agreement terms or negotiations protected.

Look for an operative prohibition on soliciting, recruiting, hiring, inducing departure, or otherwise approaching specified representatives of the disclosing party. A targeted no-contact or non-circumvention clause covering employees or other associated persons also supports the benchmark proposition when it forbids approaching them in connection with the contemplated transaction. General nondisclosure, noncompetition, or restrictions concerning customers or markets alone are unresolved. Include any lead-in supplying the actor, protected class, or duration.

Match return or destruction to a stated ending event. Termination or expiration, project or service completion, a decision not to proceed, the end of an evaluation period, or a final return at the conclusion of a temporary exchange can support the hypothesis. Thus “at the end of the evaluation period, upon request, return all materials” supports because the ending event governs the duty; “upon request” alone during an ongoing relationship is unresolved. Return alone suffices; destruction need not also appear. Include the complete trigger and every return/destruction limb.

operations.rationale: The existing rule still led the lawyer to miss annotated final-event duties while sometimes treating request-only duties as termination-triggered. The revision makes the combined ending-event/request pattern and return-versus-destruction boundary executable.

guidance.procedure: Evaluate what may remain after the stated return or destruction is completed, regardless of whether the trigger is termination or request. An express archive, backup, legal-retention, dispute, or records exception supports possession. An exhaustive command covering all protected information and copies, or alternatives such as “deliver all and cease use, or destroy and delete all,” opposes it even without saying “retain none.” A duty limited to tangible documents or another subset is unresolved. Include the governing return/destruction sentence and any retention carve-out; do not infer permission from prior possession.

operations.rationale: The lawyer repeatedly left exhaustive no-retention schemes unresolved or reversed them, despite the existing general rule. A compact alternative-performance pattern clarifies that exhaustive return-or-destroy options oppose post-return possession.

guidance.procedure: Identify an operative permission reaching recipients outside the receiving organization. Employees, officers, directors, and internal researchers alone are not third parties; consultants, advisers, contractors, agents, suppliers, affiliates, or other representatives support only when the disclosure/access clause actually authorizes them. A definition bundling such persons with a party, or a signer’s status as consultant or agent, is not permission. Thus “employees may know; no third party without consent” opposes, while “employees and consultants may receive on need-to-know terms” supports. Include the permission or ban, its continuation, and a recipient definition only when it supplies the authorized class.

operations.rationale: Across the new batch the lawyer repeatedly converted employee-only access or party definitions into outside-sharing permission, while evidence often omitted the operative lead-in. The worked contrast directly targets that persistent negative transfer.

guidance.procedure: Require both legal compulsion and an operative warning duty. The trigger and notice may be in separate sentences: “disclosure is subject to law or legal process” followed by “promptly notify the discloser of that requirement” supports. Permission to comply with law, or a compelled-disclosure exclusion without notice, is unresolved rather than contradiction. Search beyond the exception list for a later notice sentence. Include the notice provision and the complete referenced trigger sequence; exclude unrelated exclusions or generic legal-disclosure permission that does not govern the notice.

operations.rationale: The lawyer missed an explicit multi-sentence notice duty and elsewhere treated permission without notice as contradiction. The update operationalizes separated trigger-and-notice drafting and evidence membership.

guidance.procedure: Inspect the complete operative definition and ask whether its subject matter is exclusively technical. A definition consisting only of technologies, engineering material, software, designs, specifications, know-how, or comparable technical matter supports technical-only coverage even if it also describes oral, visual, written, or tangible transmission modes; a mode is not a nontechnical category. Express business, financial, commercial, personnel, customer, contractual, or marketing categories oppose. Generic “all information” or background recitals without identifiable content leave the issue unresolved. Include the definition introduction and all limbs needed to show its exhaustive content.

operations.rationale: The lawyer reversed a definition limited to technologies because oral transmission was mistaken for nontechnical content. The revised rule separates subject matter from conveyance mode and reinforces complete-definition evidence.

guidance.procedure: Test whether identification governs every protected disclosure. Universal force may arise from a lead-in such as “with respect to all protected information” followed by written marking and oral identification-plus-confirmation procedures; include that lead-in and every responsive mode-specific limb. Marking, contemporaneous designation, later confirmation, or expressly making the recipient aware can satisfy identification. Coverage whether or not marked, or based only on reasonable understanding, opposes it. General classification by an authority, the discloser merely considering information confidential, or optional labeling unconnected to coverage is unresolved.

operations.rationale: The lawyer overlooked a universal marking sequence and repeatedly omitted governing introductions or oral continuations. The update explains how a universal lead-in combines with mode-specific identification rules.

guidance.procedure: Separate survival of substantive duties from agreement duration and liability for past conduct. “These confidentiality duties survive termination” supports. A clause stating that the agreement and its obligations terminate at project completion or a fixed endpoint opposes survival when no substantive duty continues. A proviso that the recipient remains liable only for breaches committed before termination does not preserve the duties themselves; include the termination clause and endpoint limbs, not the antecedent-liability proviso alone. A fixed agreement term without either continuation or an express endpoint for the duties remains unresolved.

operations.rationale: The lawyer treated continuing liability for antecedent breaches as survival and selected that proviso instead of the operative termination sequence. This revision supplies the missing worked distinction.

guidance.procedure: Inspect whether the agreement, negotiations, contemplated project or transaction, or the fact that discussions are occurring is itself protected from announcement or disclosure. “Do not announce or disclose the project without consent,” protection of the agreement’s subject matter, and nondisclosure of negotiations or their status support the hypothesis. Confidentiality of exchanged business information, a generic entire-agreement clause, or discussion language describing purpose without protecting the discussions is unresolved. Include the operative announcement ban or the definition lead-in that makes the agreement, project, transaction, or negotiations protected; omit neighboring permissions about different facts.

operations.rationale: The lawyer missed both an operative project-announcement ban and a provision protecting the agreement’s subject matter, while overselecting neighboring transaction facts elsewhere.

guidance.procedure: Distinguish permission, prohibition, and copy-handling regulation. “May copy,” “if copies are required, make only the necessary number,” or a no-license clause preserving a right to copy solely for the purpose supports. An unqualified “shall not copy” opposes. A rule only requiring copies to retain legends, forbidding obscured markings, or controlling storage and handling leaves general permission unresolved. If an exception governs a series such as “do not copy or disclose except as necessary,” it can authorize copying within that exception. Include the undertaking lead-in when it supplies actor or force.

operations.rationale: The lawyer missed an explicit conditional permission to make necessary copies. The added pattern clarifies that a quantitative restriction can still grant copying permission while preserving the handling-rule boundary.
